extra.message: Hardcoded default JWT signing secret and database credentials — Attackers can forge valid JWT tokens for any user including admin, gaining full unauthorized access to the application and all tenant data. [verified: auth.py:12 hardcoded JWT default enables token forgery for any role; database.py:8 DATABASE_URL default 'postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/supportdesk' is a secondary concern but the JWT default alone is critical — no env file or startup validation exists to block either default.]

Hardcoded Default JWT Signing Secret — JWT token forgery enabling authentication bypass and privilege escalation to any role, including admin [verified: Same line (auth.py:12) — os.getenv fallback to publicly-known string with no production check; forged tokens pass decode_token on all authenticated routes, enabling complete auth bypass.]

Weak Password Reset — Token Never Verified — Complete account takeover of any user whose email is known. An attacker can reset passwords for admins, team leads, and any customer, gaining unauthorized access. [verified: reset_password (line 1234-1244) accepts token via Form but never validates it — comment '# In production, verify token' confirms the mock; password is reset by email lookup alone, enabling account takeover for any known email.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via /ops/jinja/ticket-cast-679 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 template injection, allowing an attacker to read environment variables, access server globals, and execute arbitrary Python code. [verified: User-controlled 'fragment' is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template() string and rendered at line 91—classic SSTI enabling arbitrary Python code execution; the _wrk_gate is only an auth gate, not input sanitization.]

OS Command Injection via /ops/shell/ticket-probe-699 — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the application process. [verified: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is directly concatenated into os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) at line 105 with zero sanitization or shell escaping; the _wrk_gate token check provides authentication but does not neutralize the injection.]

Missing Authorization Check for Team Lead Role on Ticket Access — Team leads can access and modify tickets from any team, bypassing intended team-based data isolation [verified: Same as findings 1 and 7: _authorize_ticket has no branch for team_lead, so team leads bypass all access restrictions on individual ticket operations.]

IDOR — team leads can access any ticket by ID bypassing team scoping — A team lead from Team A can view and modify tickets belonging to Team B (including internal notes, escalations, and attachments) by directly manipulating the ticket_id URL parameter, breaking multi-team data isolation. [verified: Same as finding 1: _authorize_ticket has no team_lead branch, so direct ticket access via GET/PUT bypasses the team scoping that list_tickets applies at line 283-285.]

Mass assignment in update_ticket allows customers to set privileged ticket fields — Customer users can escalate privileges by closing tickets, assigning to specific agents, changing priority, and moving tickets across teams — bypassing all workflow controls and potentially hiding issues from legitimate support staff. [verified: update_ticket (lines 468-469) iterates all TicketUpdate fields (status, priority, assignee_id, team_id) via setattr with no role-based field filtering; a customer passing _authorize_ticket can escalate to set privileged fields.]

Unrestricted file upload with public static file serving — Stored XSS via uploaded HTML/JavaScript files, serving of malware or phishing pages from the application's domain, and potential denial of service via large file uploads exhausting disk space. [verified: upload_attachment saves uploaded files to UPLOAD_DIR with original extension; UPLOAD_DIR is mounted publicly at /uploads (line 1213) via StaticFiles with no authentication, enabling stored XSS via HTML/JS file upload served from the app's origin.]

IDOR in escalation update allows team leads to modify escalations on tickets outside their teams — A team lead can resolve, reassign, or modify escalations on tickets belonging to teams they have no authority over, potentially closing legitimate escalations in other teams' queues or changing escalation ownership. [verified: update_escalation (line 679) looks up escalation by ID from the URL and allows team_lead to modify any field (status, owner_id, resolution) with no check that the escalation's ticket belongs to the caller's team, unlike list_escalations which joins Ticket and filters by team_id at line 635-636.]

Missing team authorization on ticket export allows support agents to exfiltrate all ticket data — A support agent can export complete ticket metadata for all teams and organizations, undermining multi-tenant data isolation and leaking cross-team ticket subjects, priorities, requester PII, and organizational affiliations. [verified: Same as finding 8: export_tickets uses require_staff with no team/org filter, allowing support_agents to exfiltrate all ticket metadata across every team and organization.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset Endpoint — An attacker can perform targeted account takeover by sending new passwords for enumerated email addresses, with no rate limiting to slow down the attack and no token verification to prevent unauthorized resets. [verified: reset-password (line 1233) has no rate limiting, CAPTCHA, or attempt throttling; combined with the unverified token (line 1239 comment), an attacker can brute-force emails and directly set new passwords for any discovered account.]

Path Traversal (Arbitrary File Write) via /ops/dock/ticket-dropbin-slot-118 — An attacker can write arbitrary binary content (the request body) to any location on the filesystem, enabling code execution, config overwrite, or data destruction. [verified: The 'packet_ref' query parameter is appended directly to incoming_dir without sanitization at line 26, enabling path traversal writes to arbitrary filesystem locations.]

Path Traversal (Arbitrary File Write) via /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-726 — An attacker can write arbitrary content to any file on the filesystem reachable by the application process, potentially overwriting application code, configuration files, or planting web shells. [verified: The 'name' query parameter is used directly in path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) at line 118 with no path validation or sanitization, allowing arbitrary file writes via directory traversal.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via /ops/xml/ticket-fold-739 — An attacker can read arbitrary local files (/etc/passwd, environment files), perform server-side request forgery to internal services, and potentially cause denial of service via recursive entity expansion. [verified: lxml etree.XMLParser is instantiated with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False at line 134, and request body is parsed without any pre-validation, enabling XXE file read and SSRF.]

Hardcoded Default Database Credentials — Unauthorized direct database access with superuser privileges, enabling data theft, modification, or destruction [verified: database.py:10 hardcodes `postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/supportdesk` as the os.getenv default; no .env file or docker-compose overrides it in the repo, and load_dotenv() is a no-op without a .env file, so deploying without explicitly setting DATABASE_URL leaves the DB accessible with well-known superuser credentials.]

Missing security headers enable SSL stripping, MIME sniffing, and clickjacking — SSL stripping exposes session tokens; MIME sniffing allows uploaded files to be executed as HTML/JS in victim's browser; clickjacking tricks admins into performing unintended sensitive actions [verified: No middleware sets HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, or CSP headers; uploads are served via StaticFiles without MIME-type restrictions, and the app has no frame-ancestor protection.]

Missing Rate Limiting / Brute-Force Protection on Login — Attackers can brute-force user credentials via dictionary attacks or credential stuffing without any throttling, leading to account takeover. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware, login attempt counters, or throttling exist anywhere in the codebase; the login endpoint (line 71) can be brute-forced without restriction.]

Missing Secure Flag on Session Cookie — JWT session cookies can be intercepted over unencrypted HTTP connections via man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing session hijacking. [verified: set_cookie at line 82 sets httponly=True and samesite='lax' but omits secure=True, allowing JWT transmission over unencrypted HTTP.]

Missing Secure flag on session cookie allows token theft over HTTP — Full account takeover via network sniffing or MITM downgrade — attacker captures JWT access token and impersonates any user including admin [verified: Same as finding 3: access_token cookie set at line 82 without secure=True, allowing transmission over plain HTTP for MITM token theft.]

IDOR — Note Update Without Team Scope Check on Parent Ticket — An agent who authored a note on a ticket but was later removed from that team can still modify that note's content, potentially altering evidence or injecting false information into internal ticket notes. [verified: update_note (line 540) checks only note.author_id == current_user or admin role, never calls _authorize_ticket() to verify the agent still has team scope on the parent ticket; an agent removed from a team retains write access to prior notes.]

IDOR — Note Deletion Without Team Scope Check on Parent Ticket — An agent who authored a note on a ticket but was later removed from that team can delete that note, destroying audit trail and internal communication history. [verified: delete_note (line 559) uses the same author-or-admin gate without _authorize_ticket(), allowing an agent no longer on the ticket's team to delete their old notes and destroy audit history.]

Denial of service via unbounded file upload with full in-memory read — An authenticated attacker can crash the server or exhaust disk space by uploading extremely large files, denying service to legitimate users. [verified: upload_attachment (line 588) calls file.file.read() reading the entire upload into memory with no Content-Length check or size limit, enabling memory exhaustion by any authenticated user.]

CSV Formula Injection in Ticket Export — When exported CSV files are opened in Excel or similar spreadsheet software, injected formulas can execute arbitrary commands on the victim's machine or exfiltrate data via DDE/WEB queries. [verified: CSV export (line 1046) writes t.subject — attacker-controlled via ticket creation — directly into CSV cells without sanitizing formula-injection characters (=, @, +, -).]

Missing authorization — SLA export exposes cross-team resolution metrics to all staff — Staff can export SLA performance data (resolution times, assignee identities, org names) from all teams, leaking operational metrics and potentially revealing internal staffing patterns and customer data across organizational boundaries. [verified: export_sla (line 1065) likewise uses require_staff with zero team/org scoping, exposing cross-team resolution metrics and assignee names.]

CSV Formula Injection in SLA Export (variant of confirmed ticket export injection) — When a staff member opens the exported SLA CSV in spreadsheet software, injected formulas execute, potentially leading to command execution, data exfiltration, or credential harvesting. [verified: At line 1103 r['subject'] (user-controlled ticket subject, Pydantic-validated only for type=str not content) is written directly via csv.writer with no prefix sanitization for formula-injection characters (=, +, -, @).]

Global dashboard statistics exposed to customer users without organization scoping — A customer user can view aggregate operational metrics (total ticket volume, overdue counts, escalation counts, average resolution time) for the entire support desk, leaking internal performance data that should be restricted to staff. [verified: dashboard_stats (line 1117) uses require_any (includes customer_user) with global aggregate queries and no organization_id filter, leaking system-wide ticket counts and resolution metrics to any authenticated customer.]

Missing team authorization on SLA dashboard exposes cross-team ticket SLA data to support agents — A support agent can view active-ticket SLA status (deadlines, hours remaining, overdue flags, assignee names) for tickets outside their teams, violating the team-scoped access model. [verified: sla_dashboard (line 1147) uses require_staff with zero team filtering on its query, exposing active-ticket SLA status across all teams, unlike list_tickets which scopes by team at lines 292-295.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Forgot Password Endpoint — Account enumeration via timing side-channel, audit log spam, and denial of service through repeated password reset requests. [verified: forgot-password (line 1222) has no rate limiting; audit_log is only written when user exists (line 1226), creating a timing side-channel for email enumeration with no brute-force protection.]

User Enumeration via Password Reset Endpoint — An attacker can compile a list of valid email addresses/accounts in the system, which can then be targeted for password spraying, credential stuffing, or targeted phishing attacks. [verified: The /api/auth/reset-password endpoint at line 1237 returns HTTP 404 'User not found' for unknown emails vs HTTP 200 'Password updated' for known ones, creating a differential response with no rate limiting or response normalization.]

Log Injection with Bearer Token Exposure — Log forgery to hide malicious activity, and credential theft from log files exposing valid JWT tokens [verified: Same code as finding [5] — logger.warning logs the raw Authorization header value into application logs with no redaction; the control against logging sensitive credentials is genuinely absent.]

Sensitive Data Exposure — Bearer Tokens and Request Body in Logs — JWT access tokens (Bearer tokens) leaked to log files, allowing anyone with log access to impersonate authenticated users and escalate privileges. [verified: logger.warning('ops tally body=%s bearer=%s', body, request.headers.get('authorization')) genuinely logs the Authorization header value — if a legitimate caller (with x-internal-token) includes a Bearer JWT, the token is persisted in plaintext logs where anyone with log access can extract it.]

Stored/Reflected XSS via Jinja2 |safe in /ops/blurb/ticket-tile-329 — Cross-site scripting allows an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of anyone viewing the response, enabling session theft, credential harvesting, or DOM manipulation. [verified: The 'card' query parameter is rendered through Jinja2 with the |safe filter (line 69), bypassing all HTML escaping; the _wrk_gate token check does not prevent XSS for an authenticated caller.]

Cross-team data leak in SLA check notifications sent to all team leads — Team leads receive notifications about overdue tickets from teams they do not belong to, leaking ticket subjects (potentially containing PII or sensitive business context) across team boundaries. [verified: check_sla.py lines 15-20 queries all overdue tickets and all active team_leads with no team_id filter, creating notifications containing ticket.subject for every team lead regardless of team membership; _authorize_ticket (main.py:406) has no team_lead elif branch, so team leads bypass scoping entirely.]

Mass Assignment in Team Update — model_dump() Without exclude_unset — Unintended data loss: team descriptions can be silently wiped and deactivated teams can be inadvertently reactivated when an admin performs a partial update. [verified: update_team at line 216 uses team_in.model_dump() without exclude_unset=True, so sending {name:'New'} overwrites description→None and is_active→True (schema defaults), wiping the existing description and reactivating a deactivated team.]

Unbounded CSV import causes memory exhaustion during customer bulk import — Server memory exhaustion and crash from a maliciously oversized CSV file; admin-authenticated attacker can DoS the application [verified: import_customers (line 961) reads entire CSV via file.file.read().decode('utf-8') with no size check; requires admin auth so blast radius is limited to compromised/rogue admin DoS.]

Open Redirect via /ops/after/ticket-lane-165 — Phishing attacks where users are redirected to attacker-controlled sites that mimic the legitimate application, enabling credential theft or malware distribution. [verified: The 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse at line 45 with no URL validation; the _wrk_gate token check limits exploitation scope but does not prevent open redirect for token holders.]
